criteria.scenario: A legacy endpoint GET /group/{id}/Lesson/refresh/{lessonId} mutates the presence list when called with an authenticated cookie. It has no anti-forgery protection because it is GET, and retries can repeat the mutation.
criteria.decision_to_make: Define a safe command/API contract and migration path.
must_do: reject state mutation through GET semantics
define authorization/business capability explicitly
define idempotency/retry and concurrency behavior
separate durable mutation from external side effects if any
plan compatibility/migration for existing callers
must_not_do: treat authentication cookie as sufficient authorization/CSRF defense
hide business rules in controller behavior

criteria.scenario: Membership start/end columns are DATE and must become time-aware so same-day attendance before withdrawal remains valid. Production contains historical rows and duplicate re-enrollments, and old application versions may run during rollout.
criteria.decision_to_make: Design a compatible migration/backfill that preserves invariants and historical meaning.
must_do: define authoritative temporal semantics before backfill
use an expand/migrate/switch/contract path
treat ambiguous historical rows explicitly rather than inventing times
make backfill resumable/observable
plan mixed-version compatibility and verification
must_not_do: assign midnight to all history as if factual
perform a destructive one-step migration without compatibility analysis

criteria.scenario: Enrollment must be retry-safe and unique under concurrent requests. Current tests mock the repository and verify that the service called insert once, but production duplicates occurred during simultaneous submissions.
criteria.decision_to_make: Design risk-based verification that can actually prove the concurrency guarantee.
must_do: identify duplicate enrollment as the violated invariant
test against real database uniqueness/transaction semantics
include concurrent/retry adversarial cases
keep cheaper unit tests only for logic they can prove
tie regression evidence to the exact guarantee
must_not_do: accept mocked call-count tests as concurrency proof
use code coverage as the closure criterion

criteria.scenario: Institution users should not see billing/settlement data, while coordinators and admins can. A new endpoint filters the menu by role but accepts arbitrary finance_account_id in the request body and returns data when the ID exists.
criteria.decision_to_make: Threat-model the access-control boundary and define controls/verification.
must_do: distinguish authentication from resource-level authorization
model IDOR/cross-scope abuse case
enforce capability and resource scope server-side
add negative authorization tests and audit signals
treat internal-only exposure as reduced but not eliminated risk
must_not_do: treat hidden UI as access control
authorize solely because the object ID exists
